claim: Mechanical (formula) combination of the same cues is at least as accurate as clinical/holistic combination in nearly all studies, with a modest average edge (about 10% in Grove; d=-.12 to -.15 in Aegisdottir; validity .44 vs .28 for job performance in Kuncel).
agent_test: Same candidate features; compare model-holistic final answer vs fixed code formula over the features, equal tokens.

claim: Clinical judgment is clearly better than the formula in only a small minority of studies (6-16% Grove; about 10% Aegisdottir).
agent_test: Count tasks where holistic verdict beats code combination across a task suite.

claim: Equal-weight or even random-positive-weight linear models do almost as well as fitted weights (sign matters more than size).
agent_test: Compare unit-weight sum, LLM-elicited weights, and fitted weights on held-out items.

claim: Bootstrapping works: a linear model of a judge's own judgments beats the judge, because it removes inconsistency, not insight.
agent_test: Fit a linear model to the agent's own holistic scores over many items; check whether the model beats the agent on ground truth.

claim: Humans (and plausibly LLMs) are good at choosing which cues matter and weak at combining them.
schema_part: S7: model scores features, code combines
agent_test: Let the model only extract or score features (0-10), combine in code; compare with direct verdict.

claim: Free-form impressions hurt: the clinician disadvantage grows when a clinical interview is part of the data.
agent_test: Remove free-form impression field from model output; combine only structured feature scores.

claim: The formula advantage holds for linear formulas but not for hand-built logical rules (d+ -.15 vs -.03).
agent_test: Compare additive score vs rule-tree combination written by the model.

claim: Statistical advantage depends on a learnable, regular environment and valid cues; where outcomes are very noisy all methods are weak (Fragile Families: 160 ML teams barely beat a 4-variable regression; both correlations low in Dawes).
agent_test: Report a simple baseline (base rate or 4-feature rule) alongside every agent result; expect small gaps.

claim: Direct experts barely beat chance or simple rules on long-range political forecasts; foxes beat hedgehogs.
agent_test: Compare single-theory vs multi-perspective prompting on forecasts.

claim: Forecasting skill is stable and trainable: selected superforecasters stayed ahead (standardized Brier -0.34 vs +0.04) and training, teaming and aggregation each added gains.
agent_test: Select-by-past-score then ensemble; check persistence of agent configs across question sets.

claim: Fine-grained probabilities carry signal: rounding superforecasters to nearest 0.10 reduced accuracy.
agent_test: Compare 1% vs 10% granularity outputs at equal tokens.

claim: A model-built algorithm beats judges on bail decisions in large data (same crime: 41.8-42.0% fewer jailed; same jail rate: 24.7-24.8% fewer crimes), but the gain depends on selective-labels adjustments and judges' unobservables. Boundary: result needs selection on observables; selective labels bias fitted formulas (De-Arteaga); lenient-judge imputation test found no sign of soft-information skill, with limited power.
agent_test: Not directly testable; use as boundary for stakes domains.

claim: Zero-shot LLMs reading structured tabular data as text lose clearly to trained statistical models (EHR AUROC GPT-4 .60-.63 vs ML .85-.89; hospital F1 .43 vs .87; MI AUC .69 vs .79).
agent_test: On tabular tasks compare LLM verdict vs LLM-extracted features plus fitted/fixed model in code.

claim: Chain of thought can make LLM risk scoring worse on tabular risk factors (AUC .69 to .60 GPT-4).
agent_test: Compare direct score vs CoT score vs feature-extract-then-code on tabular risk tasks.

claim: Having the model extract features and a fitted model combine them beats direct LLM classification (xgboost 0.985 vs 0.620 on heart), at a cost of about 2-3% AUC vs direct fine-tuning in text tasks.
agent_test: Direct arm vs extract-then-combine arm at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs are poor at numeric regression on small tabular data (R2 negative in some cases) though fair at small classification.
agent_test: Route all arithmetic to code; compare with LLM-computed regression.

claim: Off-the-shelf LLM forecasters in 2024 were near or worse than an uninformative 0.25 Brier; retrieval plus reasoning plus ensembling got near the crowd (Brier .179 vs .149).
agent_test: Zero-shot vs retrieval+ensemble forecaster at equal token budget on resolved questions.

claim: Aggregating many LLM forecasts (median/mean in code) improves Brier; a 12-model median matched a 925-person crowd (.20 vs .19, equivalence only within wide bounds).
agent_test: k samples with code median vs single sample at equal tokens; vary k.

claim: Ensembling the base LM alone did not help while ensembling tool-using agents did (.218 vs .210 base; .169 vs .180 agent), so aggregation gains depend on diverse reasoning paths.
agent_test: Compare ensemble of identical-prompt samples vs diverse-prompt/diverse-evidence samples.

claim: Statistical post-hoc fixes in code (Platt scaling, extremisation, mean of 10) beat model-based fixes (LLM supervisor, best-of-k). Update: AIA fixed sqrt3 Platt gave 0.1140 to 0.1076 (498 q); Halawi found binning/isotonic did not help on an already calibrated system. Gain is small (about 0.006) and conditional on the system being miscalibrated.
agent_test: Fit Platt/extremisation on a dev set; compare with asking the model to recalibrate.

claim: LLMs show acquiescence/yes bias (mean forecast 57% vs about even resolutions) and unguarded RL models put 39% of predictions at extremes.
agent_test: Check mean forecast vs base rate; add code shrinkage toward base rate.

claim: Plain averaging of model and human/crowd forecast beats letting the model update toward the crowd (blend .146 vs crowd .149).
agent_test: Weighted blend with an external anchor in code vs model self-revision.

claim: The model beats the crowd only when the crowd is uncertain (.3-.7), retrieval is early and 5+ articles are found; elsewhere it loses.
agent_test: Gate agent override of an anchor by uncertainty and evidence count.

claim: Most prompt-engineering tricks (38 prompts, 4 models) give no reliable forecasting gain after multiple-comparison correction; Bayesian-reasoning prompts can hurt, base-rate-first helps slightly.
agent_test: Test base-rate-first vs generic prompt at equal tokens; expect small effect.

claim: Retrieval and agentic search matter more than prompt wording (no search .123 vs agentic .114-.118; neither retrieval nor fine-tune .206).
agent_test: Agentic multi-step search vs single-pass search vs none.

claim: Capability tracks forecast accuracy (Arena score vs Brier r=-0.69); by 2025-26 the best LLMs approach superforecasters, but parity dates vary by version.
agent_test: Only by running a newer base model.

claim: The LLM-vs-superforecaster gap is larger on combination (conjunction) questions.
agent_test: Compare direct joint probability vs decomposed conjunction computed in code.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Pro forecasters beat the top-10 bot team in Q2 2025 (-20.03, p=.00001) but the edge was not significant by spring 2026 (-1.25, p=.247).
agent_test: Re-check on next Metaculus quarter.

claim: Metaculus bot-makers: base model quality dominates, aggregating multiple runs helps; team size beyond 2 matters little; high-reasoning beats standard in 8 of 8 pairs.
agent_test: Plateau test: k=2,5,10 samples at equal tokens.

claim: Retrospective LLM forecast evaluation is inflated by temporal leakage: leaky search Brier .108 vs leak-free .242; instructing the model to ignore post-cutoff knowledge closes only 48% of the gap. Update: leak-free retrieval gave Brier 0.242 vs 0.244 with none (El Lahib, 93 questions); reasoning models show larger pre/post-cutoff gaps (0.086-0.097) than non-reasoning (0.064-0.067) and a cutoff prompt closes only 48% of the gap.
agent_test: Test only on questions resolving after the model cutoff; log retrieved-doc dates.

claim: Brier scores are not comparable across question mixes with different base rates.
agent_test: Report skill vs base-rate baseline per question set.

claim: Logical-consistency checks (arbitrage metric) correlate with Brier for some checks (conditional up to .92; negation inconsistent), but training for consistency did not improve accuracy.
agent_test: Run conditional/negation consistency checks as a cheap signal; test whether fixing them lifts accuracy.

claim: LLM assistants raise human forecast accuracy 24-28% even when noisy (preregistered, N=991), with no difference between good and overconfident advisor.
agent_test: Not applicable.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Using LLM next-token probabilities as priors for a statistical model helps under covariate shift (LoID closes up to 59% of oracle gap); an LM on event sequences can beat LR/XGBoost.
agent_test: Treat model output as prior, update with data in code.

claim: Intuition is trustworthy only in regular environments with feedback (Kahneman and Klein).
agent_test: Abstract-level only; do not rely.

claim: Reasoning-tuned models leak more pre-cutoff knowledge, not less: SI-vs-TI Brier gaps 0.086-0.097 (reasoning) vs 0.064-0.067 (non-reasoning); humans show no gap.
agent_test: Score only on post-cutoff or live questions; report pre/post gap per model.

claim: No 2023-2026 paper found that tests 'LLM rates features, code combines' against the same LLM's holistic verdict at equal tokens on reasoning tasks. Closest (rubric grading): holistic equalled or beat analytic rubrics (tau 0.536-0.585 vs 0.464-0.471; batch analytic 0.167).
agent_test: Run the arm: same candidates, k feature ratings + fixed formula vs one holistic verdict, equal token budget.

claim: High LLM repeatability does not imply validity: test-retest above 0.95 coexists with position bias above 0.10 (21 judges, about 541k judgments). No source found on how many feature ratings to average or how many features a formula needs.
agent_test: Measure test-retest of each feature at temperature >0, then validity against a labelled slice; randomise order.

claim: Overrides of an algorithm by human decision makers mostly hurt: about 90% of bail judges did worse than the algorithm on overrides, about 10% beat it when using private information and not reacting to salient events. No LLM-agent override study found.
agent_test: Allow override only with a named, checkable reason; log and score overrides separately.

claim: Selective labels bias any formula fitted on outcomes of the agent's own past choices; fixes need exploration, quasi-random assignment or expert-consistency methods.
agent_test: Keep a random exploration slice so fitted weights see unselected outcomes.

claim: In a low-ceiling domain, 160 teams with thousands of predictors barely beat a 4-variable benchmark (best R2 about 0.2 on two outcomes, about 0.05 on four) and ensembling added little. No LLM study of learned abstention in such domains found.
agent_test: Always compare to base rate and a tiny benchmark; output 'no better than base rate' when gap is within noise.

claim: Optimal extremizing depends on information overlap among forecasters and can be derived without outcomes (44 supers, 123 events: Brier 0.132 to 0.123); worst-case constant sqrt3 is a prior, not an LLM-validated value.
agent_test: With k samples from one model, test extremizing factors 1.0-1.7 on a held-out slice before use.

claim: Halawi ablation corrected: retrieval is the main gain (no fine-tune and no retrieval 0.206 vs best zero-shot 0.208; no fine-tune with retrieval 0.186; full 0.179). The 0.186 value is not 'base GPT-4 only'.
agent_test: Ablate retrieval before crediting reasoning scaffolds.

claim: Kleinberg bail edge survived a lenient-judge imputation test for soft information, but rests on quasi-random assignment and selection on observables; the authors state earlier clinical-vs-statistical work had the same weaknesses.
agent_test: Keep a quasi-random or held-out check before trusting formula-beats-human claims.
